title: 6 ways AI can actually help with your renovation
tips: Write a clear brief
Describe the house, what you want and your budget, and ask it to turn your notes into a one-page brief. Builders can price a clear brief properly.
Compare quotes like for like
Paste in two or three quotes and ask what each one includes, leaves out or assumes. Then ask the builders about the gaps.
Decode the jargon
Lintels, Part L, damp-proof courses. Ask it to explain your survey or drawings in plain English before you meet anyone.
Try ideas before you commit
Use an image tool on a photo of your room to test layouts, colours and finishes. Great for taste, not for structure.
Plan the order of work
List the jobs and ask what usually comes first, and what might need planning permission or Building Regulations approval.
Keep a decision log
Record a voice note after each site visit and have it summarised into what was agreed. It saves arguments later.
outro: Use it as an assistant, not an expert.
Anything structural, and anything about planning or Building Regulations, gets checked by a qualified person.
caption:
AI won't build your extension, but it can make you a much better-prepared client, and that usually means a smoother job and fewer surprises.

Anything structural or about planning still needs a qualified person. If you'd like a builder who's happy to work this way, message us.

title: 6 bits of tech that make a building project run smoother
tips: Laser measure
Accurate room sizes in seconds. Fewer ordering mistakes, less waste.
Room-scanning on your phone
Newer phones can scan a room into a rough 3D plan. Handy for early ideas and for sending to designers.
Thermal camera
A phone add-on shows cold spots, missing insulation and hidden leaks before walls are closed up.
Moisture meter
Checks timber, screed and plaster are dry enough before anything is finished over them.
A shared photo thread
Weekly progress photos in one place, so owners who live away can see the job without driving down.
Leak and temperature sensors
Cheap sensors in a holiday let warn you about a leak or a cold snap while the house is empty.
outro: None of it replaces experience, but all of it helps catch problems early and keep everyone informed.
caption:
Some of the kit that helps us, and our clients, keep a job on track. The sensors are worth fitting in any holiday let that sits empty over winter.
